add.issue.name: llama-swap stats poller reloads a model right after it is unloaded

edit.description.md:
LlamaSwapStats polls `GET <host>/upstream/<model>/slots` once a second. llama-swap treats a request on its /upstream proxy as demand and loads the model, so a manual unload is undone within about a second: `/running` shows the model `starting` again right after `POST /api/models/unload`. TTL unloads stick only because the model leaves `/running` before the next poll.

Fix: poll only while the model's state is `ready`, and when llama-swap is on loopback, read `/slots` straight from the backend port listed in `/running` (`proxy`). A stopped backend refuses the connection instead of loading anything. Remote hosts keep the /upstream path, gated on `ready`.

Verify: unload the loaded model with the shell running; `/running` stays empty, and the stats still update during generation.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #262 (fix/llama-swap-stats-no-reload). Verified live with the patched file in the installed shell: after `POST /api/models/unload`, `/running` stayed empty for 20 s (before the fix it was `starting` again within half a second). A generation afterwards worked, no new /upstream slot polls appeared, and the widget had open connections to the backend port. How the stats look on screen is for review.

add.issue.name: Settings: choose render GPU (iGPU-only / dGPU) and persist across install.sh

edit.description.md:
## Problem
On a hybrid box (Intel iGPU `00:02.0` + Nvidia RTX `01:00.0`), Hyprland picks the Nvidia card as its primary renderer if a monitor is on it at login, and keeps it after unplugging. Hyprland, Xwayland, kitty, qs and Discord then hold about 840 MiB of VRAM. The operator needs the RTX card at 0 MiB for llama-swap (global rule: the GPU belongs to llama-swap only).

Today this is fixed by hand in `~/.config/hypr/custom.lua`, which `install.sh` and `aphotic update` don't overwrite:
```lua
hl.env("AQ_DRM_DEVICES", "/dev/dri/card1")
hl.env("__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES", "/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/50_mesa.json")
hl.env("__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME", "mesa")
hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "iHD")
```
`hyprland.conf` is overwritten on install, and `install.sh` appends `require("nvidia")`, which sets `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`.

## Ask
Add a Settings.qml option, "Render GPU", with these choices:
- **iGPU only**: Hyprland and all clients render on the iGPU; dGPU-attached ports go dark.
- **dGPU / hybrid**: current behaviour, Nvidia ports work.
- (optional) **Auto**: whatever Hyprland picks.

## Requirements
- Persist the choice in a generated file that install and update never overwrite, e.g. `~/.config/hypr/gpu.lua` required after `nvidia.lua`, or the existing user-state store. It must survive `install.sh` and `aphotic update`.
- Resolve the card **by PCI path** (`/dev/dri/by-path/pci-*-card`), not `cardN`. The numbering can change between boots. Note that `AQ_DRM_DEVICES` is colon-separated, so a by-path link can't be passed directly. Resolve it to `/dev/dri/cardN` at session start, or add a udev symlink without a colon.
- In iGPU mode, also override the EGL/GLX vendor and VA-API driver (above), so clients don't open `/dev/nvidia0`.
- Show in the UI that the change applies at the next login, and offer a "log out now" button.
- Detect the GPUs from `/dev/dri/by-path` and hide the option on single-GPU systems.

## Done when
- In iGPU mode after relogin, `nvidia-smi` lists no processes and shows about 0 MiB used.
- Re-running `install.sh` keeps the setting.
- Switching back to dGPU and relogging restores the Nvidia-connected output (DP-2).
- Then remove the manual block from the operator's `custom.lua`.

Ref: Qt/Quickshell API docs in `~/docs-local`.

add.issue.name: Fresh install renders icon names as text: Material Symbols missing from font cache

edit.description.md:
On a fresh install the bar, popouts and panes show glyph names ("wifi", "volume_up") instead of icons. `ttf-material-symbols-variable` is installed, but `fc-list | grep -c "Material Symbols"` returns 0 until the user runs `fc-cache -f` and restarts the shell.

Cause: install.sh installs packages one pacman transaction at a time, so the fontconfig hook runs every second or two while fonts keep landing in `/usr/share/fonts/TTF`. Fontconfig trusts a directory cache whose stored mtime matches the directory's, at one-second resolution, so a font added in the same second as the previous cache write can drop out of the cache.

Fix:
- Force a font cache rebuild once after the package lists finish, before the shell starts.
- Check that fontconfig resolves Material Symbols Rounded and warn with the fix if it does not.
- `aphotic doctor` reports the same check so affected installs can find and repair it.

add.issue.comment.md: PR #289 into dev. Reproduced the race on fontconfig 2.18.3: a font copied in within the same second as the previous cache write and followed by a plain `fc-cache` was missing in 9 of 10 runs, and `fc-cache -f` fixed it every time. The fix rebuilds both caches once after the main package list, checks the icon font, and adds an "Icon font" check to `aphotic doctor`.

add.issue.name: NVIDIA config lost on sync, and hybrid laptops get desktop-only NVIDIA settings

edit.description.md:
Reported on a Dell laptop with an Intel i7 11th gen iGPU and an NVIDIA T500 (Turing, 2 GB): the NVIDIA session settings did not seem applied.

Findings:
- `aphotic sync` / `aphotic update` run `install.sh --config-only`, which recopies `hyprland.lua` but skips NVIDIA detection, so `ISNVIDIA` is empty and the appended `require("nvidia")` is dropped. Every NVIDIA machine loses its settings after the first sync.
- Nothing detects hybrid graphics. `nvidia.lua` forces `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` on Optimus laptops where the iGPU drives the panel, and `libva-nvidia-driver` is never installed, so VA-API breaks.
- mkinitcpio loads the NVIDIA modules without `i915` first, which Hyprland's docs call out for hybrid Intel laptops (Electron/Chromium stalls after boot).
- No `prime-run`, so there is no supported way to send an app to the dGPU.

Fix:
- Detect NVIDIA (and hybrid) in the config-only path too.
- Detect an Intel/AMD iGPU next to the NVIDIA card. On hybrid, skip `require("nvidia")`, load the iGPU's kernel driver before the NVIDIA modules, and install `nvidia-prime`.
- Install `libva-nvidia-driver` on NVIDIA-only machines, where `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` stays.

Out of scope: pinning the render GPU with `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`, which belongs to 026WW1M.

add.issue.comment.md: PR #290 into dev. Fork from the original plan: hybrid is detected from connected DRM outputs, not from lspci alone. The lspci rule called any machine with both GPUs hybrid, including a desktop with the iGPU enabled and monitors on the NVIDIA card, which would have lost its NVIDIA settings. Now hybrid means a non-NVIDIA GPU drives a connected display while an NVIDIA card is present. Implementation drafted by pi/coder, reviewed and corrected by claude.

add.issue.name: CI: a local runner and log triage that agents can use

edit.description.md:
Tests that pass in a working checkout can fail in CI. The CI checkout is shallow and detached, with no `origin/main` and no gitignored files. Agents can't reproduce those failures locally, and the raw `--log-failed` output buries the one useful line under thousands of runner lines.

- `tools/ci/local.sh`: runs the required checks in a CI-shaped checkout and prints only the failing blocks.
- `tools/ci/triage.py <pr>`: splits required checks from advisory ones and prints the failing test blocks from a red run.
- AGENTS.md: a short CI section with both commands and a list of what the CI environment lacks.

add.issue.name: Decide where public contributor docs live

edit.description.md:
AGENTS.md now points agents at raw wiki pages and the plugin SDK guide. The open question: should the repo also carry a tracked docs tree that AGENTS.md links into, so a fresh clone works offline?

Options:
- **Wiki only (current).** One source, already synced to the site. Needs network, and wiki edits skip PR review.
- **Tracked tree in the repo.** Works offline and changes go through review. The name `docs/` is taken by gitignored maintainer notes, so either those move (e.g. to `.notes/`) or the public tree takes another path. Two sources of truth risk drift unless the wiki gets generated from the tree.

Also: `install.sh --help` cites `docs/exploit-layer.md`, a path users can't see.

add.issue.comment.md:
PR: https://github.com/T-Crypt/aphotic-hypr/pull/295

Scope grew by one item: AGENTS.md was gitignored, so agent worktrees had no project rules. It is now tracked as the single source; contributors copy it into CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md locally. It also links wiki pages and the plugin SDK guide by task.

Reproduced #292's CI-only failure locally with `tools/ci/local.sh`. Its fix passes.
